title: Survey Finding of Workers Being Overqualified for Their Roles and Implications on Career and Wage Progression, and Underemployment
what_it_is: Survey Finding of Workers Being Overqualified for Their Roles and Implications on Career and Wage Progression, and Underemployment

sections.label: Voluntary overqualification share
sections.summary: About nine in 10 overqualified workers, or about 17.7% of the resident workforce, were voluntarily overqualified.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Of these overqualified, about nine in 10, or about 17.7% of the resident workforce, were voluntarily overqualified.

sections.label: Involuntary overqualification rate
sections.summary: The involuntary overqualification rate was low at 1.7% of the resident workforce and stable over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In contrast, the involuntary overqualification rate was low at 1.7% of the resident workforce and has remained stable over the past decade.

sections.label: Graduate median income rise
sections.summary: Median income of full-time employed tertiary graduates rose from $5,800 to $7,600 over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If you look at the median income of full-time employed tertiary graduates over the past decade, the median incomes have risen from $5,800 to $7,600 over the 10 years, and this reflects continued wage progression.

sections.label: Overqualification data tracking
sections.summary: The Ministry has just started publishing overqualification data, as time-related measures remain the internationally accepted definition of underemployment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, if the Minister can share how the Ministry tracks long-term wage career progression outcomes for workers, especially for younger graduates who remain overqualified for extended periods, and how these insights are being used to strengthen job redesign and skills-based progression efforts across sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have just started publishing this data because this particular indicator itself on overqualification, based on what we are doing, with regard to the data, it is actually quite new.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Because up till now, based on even international published statistics, underemployment data typically use a time-related measure, and today, the time-related measure still remains the only internationally accepted statistical definition of underemployment and as a proxy, overqualification.

sections.label: SWDA targeted groups
sections.summary: With the new SWDA and the Bill's passage, focus will be on fresh graduates, mid-career workers, elderly workers and caregivers returning to work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, hopefully with your support, with the formation of the new SWDA and the passage of the Bill later on this afternoon, we will focus on initially very targeted groups – the fresh graduates, the mid-career workers, to the elderly workers, and on top of that, also for caregivers returning to work.

sections.label: Young degree holder employment
sections.summary: Employment rates among young degree holders aged 25 to 29 remained broadly stable at around 90% over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The employment rates, if you look amongst young degree holders, and let us look at that age cohort, from 25 to 29 years old, they have actually remained broadly stable – and this has been at around 90% or nine in 10 over the past decade.

sections.label: Graduate employment transition
sections.summary: Most find employment over time, indicating a longer school-to-work transition rather than a broad decline in graduate employment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Most are able to find employment over time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So therefore, this points to a longer school-to-work transition, rather than a broad decline in graduate employment.

sections.label: Career advisory and GRIT
sections.summary: The speaker hopes to work more closely with the Ministry of Education on career advisory services exposure, citing success with the extended GRIT programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We hope to work even more closely with the Ministry of Education with regard to career advisory services exposure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have got quite a good measure of success with the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) programme and I said that we have extended it this year.

sections.label: Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package
sections.summary: Beyond working with displaced workers, the speaker is working with businesses, having introduced a step-up to the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package with the SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But what we are now doing that is an even higher step-up from what we have been doing all this while, is that, beyond just working with that potentially displaced worker or that displaced worker, we are also working with the businesses as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This year at Budget Committee of Supply, if you recall, I introduced a step-up to the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package with a SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant (Job Redesign+).

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Through that, we not only fund workers in reskilling, upskilling, career guidance, enhancing Career Health SG, CareersFinder – many of these, I will talk about later on this afternoon – we are also funding companies to continue to press on with Job Redesign to improve their productivity through the Productivity Solutions Grant; through many of the enterprise development grants, which are disbursed by the economic agencies under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, which I am also closely working for.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Infocomm Media Development Authority has the TechSkills Accelerator programme.
